prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Photorealistic whole-animal anatomical target sheet, NOT illustration. Eight cells in a clear 2-row by 4-column grid, plain neutral light-grey ground, soft daylight and realistic fur. No text, labels, borders, scenery or accessories. Row1 same adult, row2 same mobile fully furred juvenile (game age0 design proxy, NOT neonatal animal); juvenile visibly smaller at SAME scale. Columns precisely: standing towards viewer, standing away, walking towards, walking away. All animals substantially side-on with a 34-degree toward/away component; camera looks DOWN 30 degrees from horizontal, long-lens near-orthographic projection. Entire animal, every foot, ear and full tail must fit each cell with generous margins. Correct four-limb anatomy, no duplication, distinct natural walking foot placement. Subject anatomy: European mole (Talpa europaea), NOT a star-nosed mole. Black velvety fur, cylindrical compact trunk with almost no visible neck, very small recessed eyes and NO external ear pinnae, long naked pink tapered snout, exceptionally broad pink shovel-shaped forehands turned OUTWARD, five toes with distinct long digging claws per forehand, tiny rear feet, short sparse-haired tail about 0.2 head-body length. Juvenile fully furred and mobile, hands still shovel-shaped. Do not substitute ordinary rodent paws.
